title: Reversionary Interest Conveyance Act
official_summary:
Reversionary Interest Conveyance Act

This bill directs the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) to offer to sell the reversionary interest of the United States in approximately 8.43 acres of land in Sacramento, California, as generally depicted on a specified map dated November 7, 2022. Within two years of receiving a request from the owner of the land, the BLM must offer the reversionary interest and convey the reversionary interest to the buyer upon payment. The payment must be in an amount that is at least the fair market value of the reversionary interest. The buyer must also pay all costs related to the applicable conveyance of the reversionary interest, including all surveys, appraisals, and other administrative costs.

The bill subjects the conveyance to valid existing rights.

The proceeds from the sale must be deposited into Federal Land Disposal Account.

summary.headline: Law lets the owner of about 8.43 acres in Sacramento, California, buy out the federal government's right to take the land back.
summary.what_it_does: The federal government holds a "reversionary interest" in about 8.43 acres of land in Sacramento, meaning it could regain the land under certain conditions. This law requires the Bureau of Land Management to offer to sell that interest to the landowner within two years after the owner asks. The buyer must pay at least fair market value plus all costs, such as surveys and appraisals, and existing legal rights to the land stay in place. The money from the sale goes into the Federal Land Disposal Account.

who_it_affects.group: The owner of the 8.43 acres in Sacramento shown on the official map
who_it_affects.how: The owner can ask to buy the federal government's right to take back the land, as long as they pay at least fair market value and all related costs.
The agency must offer the sale within two years of the owner's request and transfer the interest once payment is made.

who_it_affects.group: People or groups with existing legal rights to the land
who_it_affects.how: Their valid existing rights are protected and stay in effect after the sale.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted October 22, 2026; the BLM must make the offer within two years after the landowner requests it.
